*thinking in my own voice*

Aiyo, another year. I've been working this land since I married in, that's... 35 years now. My hands know the work better than my head. Let me think about what needs doing.

We have 16.9 mu all together, in a few plots. My man goes out to the construction site part of the year, my older son too, so mostly it's me and sometimes my daughter-in-law in the fields. That matters — I can't do everything alone, so I plant what I know how to do.

**Cotton.** This is our money crop. Our village here on the west side of the county does cotton — everyone does, so the shop has the seed, the buyers come around, we know how. I'll put 10 mu in cotton again, same plot as last year. I plant when the soil warms, around Guyu (谷雨), late April. I buy the same seed I got last year, the one the shop boss recommends, about 40-something yuan per mu worth. Before planting I put down about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that's what I always do. Then when the cotton starts putting on buds I put a bit of urea, maybe a handful per plant, something like that. I water from our tube well two or three times when it's hot and dry. I don't like to pump too much, electric is expensive and the water table keeps dropping. The hardest part comes at picking time in September-October — my daughter-in-law and I bend our backs for weeks. If there's too much I ask a neighbor woman to help for a few days, pay her cash.

For bugs, I walk the field and when I see aphids or the bollworm I go to the shop and the man there gives me the spray. I don't spray on schedule — only when I see trouble. It costs money.

**Wheat and maize.** For the family's grain, I keep 5 mu in the wheat-maize two-crops-in-one-year. The wheat went into the ground last October, it's green now and looking alright. I'll water it when it turns warm and green up — once at返青 (greening up) and again at jointing — and I put a little urea at the spring watering. Before the winter I had already given it base compound fertilizer at planting. I'll spray once for weeds, the shop has a cheap one. In June my nephew brings the combine over, one day to harvest.

Then right after — two, three days, no rest — we plant the summer maize on the same plot. My son comes back for a few days to help, or we hire the planter machine from the village. The maize is the hybrid seed, about 40 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea when it's knee-high. Water once or twice if the rain doesn't come. Spray for borer if I see it. Harvest end of September before the cotton picking gets crazy.

**Mungbean.** Small plot, less than 2 mu, by the edge. My mother-in-law always kept mungbean, I do the same. Plant after麦收 (wheat harvest), around June. Hardly any fertilizer, the beans make their own. Rainfed, I don't water it. We eat some, sell some at the market. Easy crop. I save some seed from last year.

**What's on my mind.** Money is tight this year like always. My man's construction wage helps but the boy is thinking about marrying and that costs. Fertilizer prices went up last year and I don't see them coming down. I'm not going to buy more fertilizer than I always do — can't afford to experiment. If the cotton price is bad in autumn I'll worry. If it's good, we put some aside.

I don't calculate. I do what worked before.
